<!-- markdownlint-disable MD013 -->
# seakarr

Automated Soulseek music downloader with library quality upgrading.

## Features

- **Library quality scanner** — walks your music library directories, reads audio tags (FLAC, MP3, AAC,
  OGG, Opus, WAV, WMA, and more via [lofty](https://crates.io/crates/lofty)), and identifies albums
  whose tracks are in a format outside `filters.allowed_extensions` or fall below the
  configurable bitrate threshold.
- **Automatic mode** — for each album needing an upgrade, searches the Soulseek network, ranks
  candidates by advertised speed (adjusted by measured-throughput reputation), free-slot bonus, bitrate bonus,
  album-name match and peer reliability, and downloads the best match. The result is written into your
  library when the artist already has a folder under a configured `library.paths` entry, and stays in
  `storage.staging_dir` when it does not; an album selected by `library_upgrade.enabled` is replaced in
  place. An upgrade whose every destination already holds a strictly better file
  keeps those files and still completes the album, so the staging copy is removed without a new file being
  written. A candidate whose files omit the bitrate attribute scores zero on the bitrate bonus once
  `filters.min_bit_rate` is set, so a peer that reports one is preferred; it is still admitted, because its
  real quality is verified after download.
- **Discover mode** — derives the artist list from your library (tags first,
  folder names as the fallback), keeps only the artists that own a folder of
  their own, asks MusicBrainz which conceptual albums each of those is missing,
  and downloads only those. An artist the library only knows as a guest inside
  another artist's folder is skipped, and the run summary reports how many were
  skipped that way; name one explicitly with `--artist` to process it anyway.
  Albums already present are never
  searched or re-downloaded, and each run stops after
  `discover.max_cycle_downloads` download attempts so a large library fills in
  over successive runs. Release types come from `discography.allowed_types`.
- **Manual & batch modes** — search for a specific artist/album on demand, or process a newline-separated
  text file of `artist - album` lines to download a curated wantlist.
  A run places each completed album into the artist's existing library folder when one exists
  anywhere under a configured `library.paths` entry; when the artist has no folder there, or the
  album's destination folder already exists, a manual run keeps the download in
  `storage.staging_dir` (batch and automatic runs merge into the existing folder instead, keeping
  any file that already parses as audio). An
  album-only request names no artist, so it always stays in staging and says nothing: only manual
  mode can express one, because auto mode rejects `--album` on its own and a batch line is trimmed
  before it is parsed, so a line written as `" - Album"` is read as an artist-only line. An artist-naming run with a configured library path explains a
  staging-only download once it has one.
- **Authoritative artist discography** — artist-only manual runs resolve conceptual albums from MusicBrainz
  release groups (cached locally for 30 days) and then run one sequential `Artist Album` Soulseek search per
  eligible album, oldest first. The same authoritative resolution powers `discover` mode for every artist
  it sweeps — those that own a folder named after them. Release categories and optional MusicBrainz artist IDs are configurable; the
  previous folder heuristic remains the explicit opt-out and the visible fallback.
- **Quality filtering** — filter Soulseek results by file extension, minimum
  bitrate, excluded keywords, and upload availability. With
  `download.max_queue_length: 0` a peer must offer a free upload slot; a
  positive limit also admits zero-slot peers until their reported queue
  position can be validated. Path-traversal names are rejected.
- **Peer reputation** — remembers each peer's effective throughput (bytes ÷ transfer time: retry delays plus
  the final transfer, excluding queue wait) and success rate (in SQLite), and ranks search results by a blend
  of advertised and measured throughput plus a reliability factor, so fast, reliable peers are preferred and
  slow or error-prone peers are demoted — regardless of what you search for. Controlled by
  `search.peer_reputation` (default `true`).
- **Download resilience** — speed monitoring with configurable minimums (a peer
  whose smoothed speed is below `min_upload_speed_kbps` past
  `speed_check_wait_secs` is cancelled and treated as a failed candidate rather

Both prerequisites were already loaded; preserving them. **Phase 1 complete — root cause found and evidenced. No files edited, no subagents dispatched.**

## Reproduction (deterministic, from the live runtime log)

`/cache-downloads/appdata/data/qbittorrent/completed/release/logs/seakarr.log`, run of 2026-09-22 (mode = **discover**; confirmed by the notices `discover: 1921 album(s) already present; skipped` and `discover: download budget of 200 reached`). One run processed the same album twice, 2 min apart:

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 18:17:13 | `Processing: The Beatles — Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band` (U+2019) |
| 18:18:35 | `Completed: … (13 tracks) -> …/Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band` |
| 18:19:35 | `Processing: The Beatles — Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band` (U+0027) |
| 18:20:55 | `Completed: … (13 tracks) -> …/Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band` |
| 18:43:26 | run summary lists **both** as downloaded |

Correction to the report as given to me: the live log's second title **does** contain an ASCII apostrophe — it is not "Peppers". So the real delta is U+2019 vs U+0027, and there is a *third* variant on disk.

## Evidence gathered

- **MusicBrainz genuinely holds two distinct release groups** (verified live against `musicbrainz.org/ws/2/release-group`, not just the cache): `Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band` (U+2019), `9f7a4c28-…`, 1967-05-26, Album; and `Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band` (ASCII), `e2efefb2-…`, 2009, Album. The same rows are in `discography_cache` for `the beatles`.
- **Disk now holds three spellings** under the artist folder: `Sgt. Peppers Lonely Hearts Club Band` (mtime 2026-09-06, 14 files — pre-existing), `Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band` (2026-09-22 19:18 local, 13 files), `Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band` (2026-09-22 19:20 local, 13 files, tracks suffixed "Remastered 2009").
- **The pre-existing folder's album tag is `Sgt. Peppers Lonely Hearts Club Band` with no apostrophe at all** (read from the FLAC). So the library held a *third*, archaic spelling.
- Code locations: `discography::normalize_catalog_key` (`src/discography/mod.rs:14`), `discography::normalize_album_key` (`:44`), `discover::LibraryIndex::contains_album` (`src/discover.rs:111`), `discover::missing_albums` (`src/discover.rs:409`), `discography::select_albums` (`src/discography/mod.rs:402`), `search::album_identity_key` (`src/search.rs:528`), `organizer::sanitize_component` (`src/organizer.rs:255`), `WINDOWS_RESERVED_CHARACTERS` (`src/organizer.rs:164`).

## Root cause

**Seakarr carries two different "is this the same album?" normalisers that disagree about apostrophes, and the one guarding presence and target-dedupe never folds them.**

1. `normalize_catalog_key` = NFKC → lowercase → whitespace collapse. It does **not** touch punctuation, and NFKC does **not** unify U+2019 with U+0027.
2. `normalize_album_key` = NFKC → `sanitize_component` → `normalize_catalog_key`. `sanitize_component`'s reserved set is only `< > : " | ? *` plus `/ \ \0 %`, so `'` and `’` both survive verbatim (this is why the folders on disk retain them).
3. `select_albums` dedupes MusicBrainz targets by `normalize_catalog_key(title)` (`:434`). The 1967 U+2019 group and the 2009 ASCII group key differently, so **both survive dedupe as two separate `AlbumTarget`s**.
4. `missing_albums` → `contains_album` → `normalize_album_key`. The library's only folder keyed on `sgt. peppers lonely hearts club band` (no apostrophe). Neither target's key equals that, nor each other's. So **both targets were judged missing**.
5. Both were searched independently (2309 files/115 users, then 1353 files/74 users) and both downloaded 13 tracks; the placement path took each target's title verbatim, creating two new sibling folders beside the pre-existing one.

This is **not** a stale-index artefact: even with a fresh index, step 4 still fails, because the three spellings produce three different keys.

**What is *not* at fault (negative evidence):** the search-side normaliser already folds these — `album_identity_key`/`normalize_search_term` delete `'` and drop non-ASCII, so the run's own tier-3 log line reads `Searching for Artist + Album punctuation-normalised (The Beatles Sgt Peppers Lonely Hearts Club Band)`. The duplication is purely in the presence/dedupe path, which is asymmetric with the search path.

This is **documented, deliberate behaviour**, not an oversight: `contains_album`'s comment says "Matching is a whole normalised title match, not an identity match… Punctuation stays significant by design (see the README), and the search-side `album_identity_key` heuristic is not applied here. The README documents the consequence: such a release can be downloaded again and placed beside the folder that already holds it." — and README:343/RREADME:927 state the same contract.

## Blast radius

- The latent defect is a **class**, not one album: in the cache, **1691 of 30462 release-group titles (5.5%) across 213 of 311 artists** contain an apostrophe-like character (`’ ’ ' `` ´ ʼ`) — e.g. `Beatles ’65`, `The Beatles’ Second Album`, `Keepin’ the Summer Alive`, `That’s Why God Made the Radio`, `People’s Instinctive Travels…`. Each is one variant spelling away from a fresh duplicate download.
- Adjacent near-duplicate sources in the same corpus that a broader fold would also catch: U+2010/U+2013 dashes (851 occurrences), U+2026 ellipsis (109), U+201C/U+201D curly double quotes (133).
- The live library has already accumulated 3 folders for this one album, so the current state needs a cleanup decision too.

Since the fix changes a documented cross-cutting contract (the README's punctuation-significance rule) and touches how presence, target dedupe, and possibly artist keys normalise, this needs your call before the chain plans it.

## Answer: the artist-side concerns I raised are **not real** — and the benefit is real and evidenced

I checked both directions with live data rather than reasoning.

**Risk side — no collisions found:**

- Live MusicBrainz artist search: `Guns N' Roses` → 5 artists, 5 distinct apostrophe-folded keys, **0 collisions**. Same for `Guns N Roses`, `Sinéad O'Connor`, `T'Pau`. Folding apostrophes would not merge two genuinely different artists anywhere I could find.
- The one collision that *did* appear — `The Beatles` returning 5 distinct MBIDs — is five artists literally all named "The Beatles" (the real band, a SiIvaGunner collaboration, a punk/lofi act, a 1960s doo-wop group, a Ukrainian act). That is a **pre-existing disambiguation problem** that exists with or without apostrophe folding, and seakarr already handles it via its "uniquely dominant score" rule. Folding doesn't make it worse.
- Your own cached discography: 311 artists, **0** with an apostrophe in the name, **0** MBIDs that folding would merge.

**Benefit side — the gap is real, and it is already mis-matching your library:**

| Your library folder | Current key | MusicBrainz canonical name | MB key after fold |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Guns 'n' Roses` | `guns 'n' roses` | `Guns N’ Roses` (U+2019) | `guns n roses` |
| `Fun Lovin' Criminals` | `fun lovin' criminals` | `Fun Lovin’ Criminals` (U+2019) | `fun lovin criminals` |

Under `resolve_artist` (`src/discography/mod.rs:175-178`), resolution accepts only a candidate whose `normalize_catalog_key` **equals** the library key. `guns 'n' roses` ≠ `guns n' roses`, so those artists cannot resolve — they land in the `30 artist(s) unresolved on MusicBrainz` bucket or get skipped. (`Plump DJ's` is the same shape: MusicBrainz has `Plump DJs`, folding gives `plump djs` = your folder's folded key.)

So the important discovery: **MusicBrainz's own canonical artist names use U+2019** (`Guns N’ Roses`, `Fun Lovin’ Criminals`). Artist-side apostrophe folding is therefore not a risky behaviour change — it is a **bug fix** that lets exact-match resolution work for names MusicBrainz spells typographically. The concerns I flagged were theoretical; the counter-evidence says the risk is negligible and the upside is concrete for your library.

## Recorded so far

1. **Fold scope → reuse `album_identity_key`** for album presence + target dedupe.
2. **Existing dupes → prevent recurrence only** (no auto-merge/delete of your folders; the three Sgt. Pepper folders stay for you to consolidate).
3. **Artist keys → still open** (your question above).

## What your album choice (#1) actually implies — from reading the code

- It **does** fix this bug: all three spellings collapse to `sgt peppers lonely hearts club band`, because `album_identity_key` routes both through `normalize_search_term`, which deletes `'` and drops non-ASCII. Your own run already proved this — tier 3 logged `Searching for Artist + Album punctuation-normalised (The Beatles Sgt Peppers Lonely Hearts Club Band)`. Both MusicBrainz groups (1967 U+2019, 2009 ASCII) then dedupe to one target.
- **Editions stay distinct**, which protects the README's deluxe/remastered rule: `strip_bracketed_annotations` (`src/search.rs:474`) *preserves* any bracket containing an `ALBUM_EDITION_KEYWORDS` word, so `Days to Come (Deluxe Edition)` keeps a different key from `Days to Come`.
- **Self-titled albums are safe**: when artist-prefix stripping empties the token list, the function returns the pre-strip fallback (`normalized_fallback`), i.e. the title itself — not the artist identity (`src/search.rs:594-599`).
- **Two consequences the plan must handle**, both real:
  - It also strips bare release years, format labels (`FLAC`, `320`) and non-edition brackets, so presence becomes more permissive than today — a library folder `Days to Come FLAC` would now satisfy target `Days to Come` and no longer be re-downloaded. That is the direction you want, but it contradicts README:343/RREADME:927 and needs a README update.
  - `select_albums` (`src/discography/mod.rs:402`) has no `artist` parameter, but `album_identity_key` needs one for prefix stripping. The artist must be threaded into that call site — an implementation detail for the plan, not a blocker.

## Phase 1 complete — root cause identified, decisions recorded

**Markers preserved:** `Harness status: loaded.` · `Project context status: loaded.`

### The bug, in one sentence

Seakarr carries **two disagreeing normalisers for "is this the same album?"** — the search side (`album_identity_key`) folds apostrophes; the presence/dedupe side (`normalize_catalog_key` / `normalize_album_key`) does not — so three spellings of one album (`Sgt. Peppers`, `Sgt. Pepper’s` U+2019, `Sgt. Pepper's` ASCII) became three distinct albums, two of them downloaded in a single discover run.

### Evidence chain (all verified, nothing inferred)

1. **Runtime log** (`…/release/logs/seakarr.log`, discover run of 2026-09-22): `Processing` → `Completed` twice, 18:18:35Z and 18:20:55Z, into two sibling folders; summary at 18:43:26Z lists both. The paste I was given was inaccurate — the live log's second title has an ASCII apostrophe, not "Peppers", and a **third** no-apostrophe variant exists on disk.
2. **MusicBrainz genuinely has two release groups** (live API, not just cache): `Sgt. Pepper’s…` U+2019 `9f7a4c28-…` (1967-05-26) and `Sgt. Pepper's…` ASCII `e2efefb2-…` (2009).
3. **`select_albums` dedupes by `normalize_catalog_key`** (`src/discography/mod.rs:435`) → both targets survive.
4. **`contains_album` → `normalize_album_key`** (`src/discover.rs:111`, `src/discography/mod.rs:44`) → the library's tag key `sgt. peppers lonely hearts club band` (read from the FLAC) matches neither target → both judged missing.
5. **`sanitize_component` does not strip apostrophes** (`WINDOWS_RESERVED_CHARACTERS` is only `< > : " | ? *`), so the variants persist on disk.
6. This is **documented deliberate behaviour**, not an oversight — `contains_album`'s comment and README:343/927 state that punctuation stays significant and the consequence is re-downloading beside an existing folder. Your request changes that contract.
7. **Class, not one album:** 1691/30462 cached release-group titles (5.5%, 213/311 artists) contain apostrophe-like characters. 293/3003 of your library directories do too.
8. **Artist side:** live probes found **0** fold collisions; MusicBrainz's own canonical names use U+2019 (`Guns N’ Roses`, `Fun Lovin’ Criminals`), so artist folding *fixes* resolution your library currently fails.

### Decisions recorded for the fix step

| Decision | Choice |
|---|---|
| Album presence + target-dedupe key | **Reuse `album_identity_key`** |
| Artist identity keys | **Fold apostrophes too** |
| Existing duplicate folders | **Prevent recurrence only** — no auto-merge/delete |

### Carried forward to the plan/implement step (not done here)

- Thread `artist` into `select_albums` (`src/discography/mod.rs:402`) so `album_identity_key` can be used there.
- Keep bundle detection and sort keys on `normalize_catalog_key` — only the comparison points change.
- README must be updated at the punctuation-significance paragraphs (343 and 927); verify `(Deluxe Edition)` brackets stay distinct (they do — `strip_bracketed_annotations` preserves edition keywords).
- Not yet verified by execution: the exact key equality for the three Sgt. Pepper spellings under `album_identity_key`. Code reading plus the run's own tier-3 log line (`Sgt Peppers Lonely Hearts Club Band`) both indicate they unify, but that must be **pinned by a failing-then-passing test** in the TDD step, along with the `Guns 'n' Roses` ↔ `Guns N’ Roses` artist case.

def test_start(text):

prod = {}

    m = re.match(r'^@@ -(\d+)(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)(?:,\d+)? @@', line)
    if m:
        old_no, new_no = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))
        continue
    if cur is None: continue
    if line.startswith('+') and not line.startswith('+++'):
        prod.setdefault(cur, {'add':0,'del':0,'new':[]})
        prod[cur]['new'].append((new_no, line[1:])); new_no += 1
    elif line.startswith('-') and not line.startswith('---'):
        prod.setdefault(cur, {'add':0,'del':0,'new':[]})
        prod[cur]['del_new'].append((old_no, line[1:])) if 'del_new' in prod[cur] else prod[cur].setdefault('del_new',[]).append((old_no, line[1:]))
        old_no += 1

def is_code(t):
    s = t.strip()
    if not s: return False
    if s.startswith('//') or s.startswith('///') or s.startswith('//!') or s.startswith('#'): return False

    dele = sum(1 for ln,t in d.get('del_new',[]) if ln < ts_old and is_code(t))
    total += add + dele

result.output:
## Review

**Scope reviewed:** the full change set in `/tmp/code-review-full.diff` (1685 lines, 6 files: `README.md`, `src/client.rs`, `src/db.rs`, `src/discography/mod.rs`, `src/discover.rs`, `src/main.rs`), which I cross-checked against `watchdog_diff --stat` (identical file set, 1065 insertions) and against the current contents of the touched files plus the seams they call into (`src/search.rs`, `src/organizer.rs`, `src/scanner.rs`, `src/discs.rs`, `src/runner.rs`, `src/config.rs`, `src/scan_progress.rs`, `src/test_support.rs`, `src/lib.rs`). I read the code, not the summary. No shell was available, so nothing was executed — test commands for the supervisor are listed at the end.

**No P0 or P1 issue found.** The core change is sound: `contains_album`/`build_index` and `select_albums` now share `search::album_identity_key`, which is exactly the seam that produced the operator's double download, and the production seam/ordering guarantees in `run_with` are intact. The findings below are P2 (report-only): two README statements that the code contradicts, three edge cases introduced by the folding choice, and test-quality/observability defects.

### Findings

1. **P2 — `README.md:343-345`: "a leading or trailing release year" is not what the code does, and the README contradicts itself.**
   `album_identity_key` strips only a *leading* bare year (`search.rs:393-405`), a bracketed year (`search.rs:434-443`), a separator-enclosed interior year (`search.rs:465-475`), an ISO date, and the special self-titled case ("Artist 1998"). A bare *trailing* year stays in the key: `album_identity_key("Days to Come 2006", "Bonobo")` = `days to come 2006` ≠ `album_identity_key("Days to Come", "Bonobo")` = `days to come`. The same README states the opposite 670 lines later: `README.md:1017-1018` "a trailing bare year stays significant to avoid merging `Blade Runner` with `Blade Runner 2049`" — and that FAQ text is the accurate one. Why it matters: an operator relying on the new presence paragraph expects a peer folder named `Days to Come 2006` to count as present, and instead gets the album re-downloaded every run — the exact failure class this change was made to stop. Smallest fix: drop "or trailing", or reword to "a leading or bracketed release year (`2006 - Days to Come`, `Days to Come (2006)`)".

2. **P2 — `README.md:346-347` ("bracketed text that names no edition") is misleading, and the behaviour it hides can silently skip a release.**
   `strip_bracketed_annotations` (`search.rs:477-496`) preserves an annotation only when one of its words is in `ALBUM_EDITION_KEYWORDS` (`search.rs:81-106`), which contains no `bonus`, `tracks`, `disc`, `box`, `b-sides`, `ep`, `soundtrack`. So `Album (Bonus Tracks)`, `Album (Disc 2)` and `Album (B-Sides)` fold to the plain `Album` key (the same fold is pinned by the repo's own test at `search.rs:2200-2210` for `(bonus disc)`). Because presence now uses that key (`discover.rs:118-152`), a library that holds only `Album (Bonus Tracks)` makes the plain MusicBrainz `Album` look present and discover **never downloads it** (and vice versa), while `README.md:351-358` promises the opposite for editions. Smallest fix: reword the paragraph to "bracketed text whose words are not in the edition list" (or add the missing words to the list if that fold is not intended).

3. **P2 — `src/discography/mod.rs:436-468`: the new identity dedupe drops a release group with no log at all.**
   Before this change each distinct raw title produced one target; now `album_identity_key` collisions (`mod.rs:436`) keep only the "better" candidate (`mod.rs:447-468`) and the loser disappears silently — no `tracing::debug!`, unlike every other rejection in that function (`mod.rs:433`, and `log_rejected_release`). Because the identity also folds bracketed non-edition annotations (finding 2), `Days to Come` and `Days to Come (bonus disc)` are now one target and the second is never searched or downloaded, with nothing in the run output to explain the disappearance. Smallest fix: emit a `tracing::debug!` naming the dropped `release_group_id` and title when `better(...)` is false.

4. **P2 — `src/discography/mod.rs:30-40`: the apostrophe filter runs *before* NFKC, so compatibility spellings of the same mark survive the fold.**
   `APOSTROPHE_LIKE_CHARACTERS` is filtered off the raw string, and only then is `.nfkc()` applied. NFKC maps `U+FF07` (fullwidth apostrophe) to ASCII `U+0027`, which is never filtered, so `normalize_catalog_key("Guns N\u{FF07} Roses")` = `guns n' roses` while `normalize_catalog_key("Guns N' Roses")` = `guns n roses` — two keys for one artist/album spelling, i.e. the same miss this change exists to remove (a non-ASCII keyboarded tag does not resolve and the album is re-downloaded). `normalize_album_key`, which this diff deleted, deliberately folded *before* the sanitiser for exactly this class of reason. Smallest fix: fold first, then filter, then lowercase (`value.nfkc().collect::<String>()` → filter → `to_lowercase`).

5. **P2 — `src/discover.rs:371-386` vs `src/discover.rs:118-152`: dropping the sanitiser fold reintroduces a presence miss for titles the sanitiser rewrites.**
   The old `normalize_album_key` folded both sides through `sanitize_component`; the new code compares the raw target title against keys built from the on-disk (sanitised) folder name. `sanitize_component` *removes* `<>:"|?*` and control characters (fusing words) and replaces `/`,`\` with `-`, `%` with U+FF05, `..` with U+FF0E, and an all-unsafe name with `_` (`organizer.rs:159-225, 255-272`). `album_identity_key` mostly reproduces that by tokenising, but not for unspaced removals or an all-stripped title: `album_identity_key("???", "A")` = `???` while the folder the write path created keys as `album_identity_key("_", "A")` = `_`; likewise `Album:Two` (folder `AlbumTwo` → `albumtwo`) vs target `album:two` → `album two`. Consequence: for such a title the placement is never recognised as present and discover re-downloads it every cycle (charged against `discover.max_cycle_downloads`). Trigger is narrow (a title whose characters are exactly the sanitiser's removal set, or one of them unspaced), but it is a regression caused by this diff. Smallest fix: keep a sanitiser-folded fallback key alongside the identity (`contains_album` also testing `album_identity_key(&sanitize_component(title), artist)`).

6. **P2 — `src/main.rs:258-262`: `let _ = …try_init();` discards the installation failure.**
   `init()` panicking on a second call is a real problem for the new tests, but `try_init` is now silent in both directions: if the global subscriber cannot be installed, the process runs with **no console output and no file log** and no diagnostic at all. Production cannot reach that today (only `run_with` installs a subscriber; `test_support`'s capturing subscriber is `#[cfg(test)]`-gated, `lib.rs:25-26`), but this is the kind of silent loss an operator cannot debug. Smallest fix: `if let Err(error) = …try_init() { eprintln!("seakarr: logging subscriber was not installed: {error}") }`.

7. **P2 — `src/main.rs:1913-1926` (`the_installed_console_filter_toggles_the_scan_heartbeat`) cannot fail for the reason it claims.**
   `install_console_filter` is a `OnceLock` set-once (`scan_progress.rs:26-38`), and the crate's own lib-side test asserts "no test may install the process-wide console filter" (`scan_progress.rs:235-246`) — so the handle this test toggles is whichever `run*` test won the race in the bin's test process (possibly one whose `reload::Layer` was dropped because *its* `try_init` lost). The reload closure swallows every failure by design (`main.rs:264-272`), and the test asserts nothing about the effect, so it passes whether the filter is live or dead. Smallest fix: assert something observable (e.g. capture the `console_handle.modify` result, or expose the reload state) or drop the claim from the comment.

8. **P2 — `src/main.rs:1027-1050` (`a_discover_plan_dispatches_to_the_discover_runner`): the stated precondition is false and one assertion is vacuous.**
   The comment and the `expect_err` message say the plan is refused because no discography is configured, but the fixture never disables it — `Config::default().discography.enabled == true` (`config.rs:269`), and `run_discover_mode` checks `discography.enabled` *first* (`runner.rs:2260-2264`) and `library.paths.is_empty()` second (`runner.rs:2265-2268`), so the error actually comes from the cleared library paths. `assert!(!error.to_string().is_empty())` cannot fail for any error here. Smallest fix: either set `config.discography.enabled = false` and assert the message contains `discography.enabled`, or keep the empty library and assert it contains `library.paths is empty`.

9. **P2 — `src/main.rs:1801-1815`: the new child-process test lost the kill-on-timeout its sibling has.**
   `schedule_handles_real_signals_and_removes_pid_file` kills and reaps the child before failing (`main.rs:1104-1118`); the new test calls `child.wait().unwrap()` directly after `receive_child_marker(..., 30s)` returns false. The child loops `select!{ scheduled / sleep(25ms) }` until `searches > 0`, so if the scheduled run ever stops issuing searches without completing, the parent blocks forever and the whole bin test binary hangs (the child also keeps its PID file alive). Smallest fix: `let _ = child.kill(); let _ = child.wait();` before the `assert!(stopped, …)`, as the sibling does.

10. **P2 — `src/main.rs:1947-1953`: the ordering assertion cannot observe ordering.**
    `dir/db/seakarr.db.is_file()` with the message "the database is opened before the PID lock is taken" is true in either order (both the DB file and a released PID file exist after login fails). The ordering claim is instead pinned only by the comment at `main.rs:282-283` ("DB errors should not leave a stale pid") and by the code order I verified at `main.rs:275-286`. Smallest fix: make the inverse explicit — a test where `database.path` is a file so `Database::open` fails, asserting `pid/seakarr.pid` does not exist (that also pins the stale-lock behaviour the comment promises).

11. **P2 — `src/client.rs:1093-1104` and `src/client.rs:1107-1130`: both source-text guards still match production strings, but each is weaker than its message.**
    Verified: `"RealClient::from_config("` occurs exactly once in `main.rs` (`main.rs:189`, inside `real_client_factory`, reachable only through `run(cli)` at `main.rs:192-194`), and `"client.apply_max_peers"` occurs exactly once (`main.rs:322`), with the window correctly terminated by `config.schedule.enabled` (`main.rs:341`) and containing the real `release_pid_lock` call (`main.rs:325-328`). But (a) after the refactor guard 1 no longer proves *`run`* uses that factory — a change to `Box::new(|_| Box::new(RealClient::new()))` in `run()` would still pass it; (b) guard 2 is satisfied by any occurrence of the text `release_pid_lock` in the window, including one placed after `return Err(e);` (which compiles with an unreachable-code warning). Smallest fix: anchor guard 1 on `run_with(cli, Box::new(real_client_factory))` and guard 2 on the ordered substring `release_pid_lock(&pid_file) {\n … }\n        return Err(e);`, or replace both with the executable tests that now exist (`run_releases_the_pid_lock_when_the_peer_cap_is_rejected`, `main.rs:1846`).

12. **P2 — `src/client.rs:1880-1893` duplicates `src/client.rs:1060-1073`.**
    `from_config_takes_the_login_retry_policy_from_the_configuration` and `login_retry_policy_comes_from_configuration` build the same fixture and assert the same two fields (`login_retries == 7`, `login_retry_delay_secs == 11`). Harmless, but the new one adds no coverage; the *new* value would be asserting the observed fields through the production factory (`real_client_factory`), which is the seam guard 1 can no longer protect.

13. **P2 (residual risk, report-only) — the artist-key apostrophe fold widens several non-obvious matches.**
    `normalize_catalog_key` now drives: `discover.exclude_artists` matching (`discover.rs:select_artists`, documented at `README.md:330` as "ignoring case and spacing" only), `discography.artist_mbids` validation where duplicate-key rejection can now **reject a config that used to load** (`config.rs:876-883`), `resolve_artist`'s candidate filter (`discography/mod.rs:165-184`) — so two MusicBrainz artists whose names differ only by an apostrophe-like character both match and are resolved by score dominance instead of being reported ambiguous — and the discography/failure caches keyed on `artist_key` (existing rows keep the pre-fold key, so one extra MusicBrainz lookup per apostrophe-bearing artist after upgrade). I could not name a concrete pair of genuinely different artists that this merges, and the direction of the trade is correct for the reported bug, so this is a note rather than a defect. Smallest mitigations: update `README.md:330` and the `exclude_artists` doc line, and consider a one-line migration/comment for cache keys.

### Verified correct (so the notes above are the whole delta)

- **Reported symptom is genuinely fixed at both seams.** `Sgt. Peppers LHCB` (library tag, no apostrophe) now shares one `album_identity_key` with both MusicBrainz spellings, so `contains_album` reports it present *and* `select_albums` collapses the 1967/2009 release groups into one target (the same-run duplicate cannot recur even on an empty library). The new tests are non-vacuous: `discover.rs:1206-1251` fails on the pre-change code (old `normalize_album_key` kept `’`), and `discography/mod.rs:1470-1520` fails with two albums.
- **Edition markers stay significant for every listed word**, unbracketed and bracketed: `Album (Deluxe Edition)` → `deluxe edition`, `Album (Live)` → `album live`, `Album [Remastered]` → `album remastered`, `Album Acoustic` → `album acoustic`, while plain `Album` → `album`. `strip_structural_words` only removes `album(s)` when ≥2 other words remain, so "Album" itself keeps its identity.
- **The artist argument added to `album_identity_key` cannot silently mismatch the index**: every spelling pair the pipeline can produce agrees in `canonical_artist_words` (checked `Guns N’ Roses`/`Guns 'n' Roses`/`Guns N Roses`, `The Beatles`/`Beatles`, `AC/DC`/`AC-DC`, `Kruder & Dorfmeister`/`Kruder Dorfmeister`), and discover passes the library's own spelling (`runner.rs:2513` ← `select_artists` / `artist_name`), not the MusicBrainz canonical name.
- **`main.rs` refactor is safe in production**: `main` → `run(cli)` → `run_with(cli, Box::new(real_client_factory))` → `RealClient::from_config` (`main.rs:140, 189, 192-194`); the factory receives the post-`merge_cli` config (`main.rs:207-228`, `303`); the DB is still opened *before* the PID lock (`main.rs:275-286`); every post-lock early return releases the lock (login `main.rs:310-320`, peer cap `main.rs:323-330`, dispatch `main.rs:357-368`, schedule via `run_schedule` `main.rs:586-606`). The one `?` after the lock — `schedule_interval(interval_mins)?` (`main.rs:342`) — is unreachable because `config.validate()` runs earlier (`main.rs:270`) and rejects the same bound (`config.rs:920-925`).
- **Trait upcasting `&dyn StartupClient → &dyn SoulseekClient` (`main.rs:334`) is fine**: MSRV is declared `1.88` (`Cargo.toml:9`) and upcasting stabilised in 1.86.
- **No new security surface**: the diff builds no path from peer data (`album_identity_key`/`normalize_catalog_key` results are map and DB keys only), fixtures contain only fake credentials (`test-user`/`test-pass`), and the new `db.rs`/`client.rs` tests leak nothing. Log injection via peer filenames is untouched.
- **`db.rs` new tests are consistent with the code** (`Database::open` message `cannot create db dir` at `db.rs:85-86`; `is_album_processed` is `COLLATE NOCASE` at `db.rs:262-274`, so the case-differing assertions hold; the read-only migration error is `SeakarrError::Database` via `execute_batch`). I could not execute them.

**Merge verdict: OK with notes.** No blocker; findings 1, 2 and 3 are the ones worth fixing in the same change (two are documentation that promises behaviour the code does not have, one is a silently dropped release group), and 4-5 are cheap one-line/one-helper fixes.

**Commands the supervisor must run** (no shell was available to me):
- `cargo test --workspace` — everything, including the two child-process tests.
- `cargo test --bin seakarr -- --exact tests::run_with_a_scheduled_plan_releases_the_pid_lock_on_a_real_signal --nocapture` — the new signal test in isolation (findings 9/10 live here).
- `cargo test --lib discography::tests::release_groups_of_one_album_are_deduplicated_by_identity discover::tests::an_album_held_under_an_apostrophe_less_tag_satisfies_both_musicbrainz_spellings` — the two regression tests that pin the reported bug.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` — `let _ = …try_init()` and the unreachable-code scenario in finding 11.

Note: on review-only/no-edit instructions I made no edits and wrote no `progress.md`; no repository or staged state was touched.

Based on my thorough review of the diff and surrounding code, here are my findings:

## Review

### Correct (with evidence)
- **The core bug fix works**: `album_identity_key(album, artist)` in `src/discover.rs:120,373,384` and `src/discography/mod.rs:436` collapses the apostrophe variants of "Sgt. Pepper's", "Sgt. Pepper’s" (U+2019), and "Sgt. Peppers" into one identity key. The reproduction test `an_album_held_under_an_apostrophe_less_tag_satisfies_both_musicbrainz_spellings` (discover.rs:1207) and the upstream `release_groups_of_one_album_are_deduplicated_by_identity` (discography/mod.rs:1466) pin this end-to-end.
- **Edition markers stay distinct**: `ALBUM_EDITION_KEYWORDS` in src/search.rs:143 is preserved by `strip_bracketed_annotations` (src/search.rs:481-490); `edition_markers_keep_an_album_distinct_from_the_plain_title` (discover.rs:1521) pins the contract.
- **PID lock release on every early return after acquisition**: Login-failure branch (main.rs:315-322), apply_max_peers-failure branch (main.rs:325-331), and the non-schedule dispatch (main.rs:362-364) all release. The schedule branch only releases on signal (intentional). The new source-text guard `main_releases_the_pid_lock_when_client_setup_fails` (client.rs:1102) covers the seam between `client.apply_max_peers` and `config.schedule.enabled`.
- **Database opens before PID lock**: Order in `run_with` is `Database::open` (main.rs:285) before `acquire_pid_lock` (main.rs:298), asserted by `run_releases_the_pid_lock_when_the_login_fails` (main.rs:1932-1952).
- **`try_init()` does not panic** in tests that drive `run` more than once; behavior is documented at main.rs:258-262.
- **No security issues**: Peer-supplied filenames flow through statically-initialized regexes in `album_identity_key`; `try_init` discards a second-subscriber error rather than panicking.

### Findings

1. **P2 — README at `README.md:953` is now inaccurate**: Says "Conceptual albums are deduplicated by normalized title and processed oldest first, so different editions or remasters of the same album produce one targeted search". The new code dedupes by `album_identity_key` (src/discography/mod.rs:436), which is more aggressive (year/format/artist-suffix folded) and explicitly **keeps** edition markers distinct — so the README's stated consequence ("different editions or remasters … produce one targeted search") is the opposite of the new behavior. Either the prose or the dedupe target should be reconciled.

2. **P2 — README at `README.md:330` (`exclude_artists`) understates the folding**: Says "matched as whole names ignoring case and spacing", but `normalize_catalog_key` (src/discography/mod.rs:38) now also strips `'` `\u{2018}` `\u{2019}` `\u{201B}` `\u{02BC}` `` ` `` `\u{00B4}`. An operator spelling "Bobs" would silently match "Bob's" via the exclusion list.

3. **P2 — README edition-marker list at `README.md:351-354` is incomplete vs the code**: README lists "deluxe, remastered, limited, anniversary, expanded, live, acoustic, instrumental, demo, remix, single, session, tour, part, mixtape". The actual `ALBUM_EDITION_KEYWORDS` (src/search.rs:143-168) also matches `remaster`, `edition`, `reissue`, `special`, `collector`, `version`, `remixes`, `sessions`. The README should match the code so users can predict which annotations get preserved.

4. **P2 — Artist-identity paragraph at `README.md:360-363` omits `backtick` and `acute accent`**: The README says "folds case, width and apostrophes", but the code's `APOSTROPHE_LIKE_CHARACTERS` (src/discography/mod.rs:22-25) also removes `` ` `` (U+0060) and `´` (U+00B4). Same exclusion-mismatch concern as #2.

Combined with `album_identity_key` (the only thing `contains_album` and `build_index` consult for albums now), this means two releases that share the same conceptual album only on the numeric-form folder spelling will silently merge in the presence index, while releases on the spelled-out form will not. 6. **P2 — `the_installed_console_filter_toggles_the_scan_heartbeat` (main.rs:1922) passes vacuously under test-ordering**: If any prior test in the same binary has already installed a global subscriber, the `try_init()` at main.rs:262 silently returns Err; `install_console_filter` still records the `Arc<ConsoleFilterFn>` holding a `reload::Layer` whose handle is unreachable from any tracing machinery, so `set_console_heartbeat(false/true)` (main.rs:1927-1928) are no-ops that still satisfy the assertions. No bug, just worth confirming the round-trip is preserved; the existing `bundle_log_fixture` test does not exercise an apostrophe-containing bundle.

- **a)** `normalize_catalog_key` filters apostrophes on **both** sides of NFKC (`src/discography/mod.rs:23-50`); `U+FF07` → `U+0027` is caught by the post-NFKC filter, so the round-2 test `catalog_keys_fold_a_compatibility_variant_of_the_apostrophe` is real. - **b)** `presence_keys` (`src/discover.rs:78-90`) is symmetric: the index entry stores both `identity` and `sanitised` (when they differ), and the query side probes both. The fused-title case (`Album:Two` ↔ `AlbumTwo`) and the placeholder case (`???` ↔ `_`) round-trip in either direction. Two genuinely different albums cannot over-merge because the **identity** key, not the sanitised one, is the primary gate, and the two albums in the worry case must differ in some non-sanitiser-stripped character to keep different identities.
- **c)** `select_albums` now emits a `tracing::debug!` for the dropped release group (`src/discography/mod.rs:470-481`); the recording carries both the loser's and the keeper's MBID.
- **d)** `main.rs:254-269` now uses `try_init` and reports a failure to stderr instead of swallowing it.
- **e)** README: trailing-year claim, edition-list enumeration, "Discovery" dedupe paragraph, `exclude_artists` row, and the artist-identity apostrophe paragraph are all consistent with the code I read.
- **f)** Test-quality fixes are all present and load-bearing:
  - `main_builds_the_client_from_configuration` now asserts both the call-site call (`run_with(cli, Box::new(real_client_factory))`) and the factory definition (`RealClient::from_config(`).
  - The order assertion `released < returned` for the rejected-cap branch is a real positional check on the source.
  - The console-filter test comment explicitly disclaims what it does **not** prove.
  - The discover-plan test asserts the actual refusal message ("library.paths is empty").
  - The signalled child kills the child on timeout.
  - `the_database_is_opened_before_the_pid_lock_is_taken` proves the ordering.
- The round-1 disc-marker asymmetry claim is correctly rejected by `strip_bracketed_annotations` — `(Disc 1)` is peeled by `strip_embedded_disc_marker` and `(Disc One)` by the bracket-stripper because "one" is not in `ALBUM_EDITION_KEYWORDS`.

On Linux, `OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true).open(directory)` fails the syscall with `EISDIR`, which Rust maps to `io::ErrorKind::IsADirectory`, **not** `AlreadyExists`. The match in `acquire_pid_lock` (`src/main.rs:478-528`) only special-cases `AlreadyExists`; every other error falls into `Err(e) => return Err(e.into())`, producing `SeakarrError::Io(_)`. The first assertion fails; the second (`pid_file.is_dir()`) passes. The comment on line 1013 ("create_new reports AlreadyExists") documents the wrong assumption. Smallest fix: either (i) extend the match in `acquire_pid_lock` with `Err(e) if e.kind() == ErrorKind::IsADirectory || e.kind() == ErrorKind::PermissionDenied => return Err(SeakarrError::PidLock(...))`, or (ii) stat the path before `create_new` and pre-empt the directory case. The test still exercises the negative-cache and Disconnected-surfacing paths correctly, but the "fast because unusable address" justification is wrong — it is fast because address parsing fails, which is even faster than a connect-timeout but for a different reason. A reader debugging a future slowness regression here will be misled.

On Linux, the kernel returns `EISDIR` before `O_EXCL` is even evaluated; `create_new` does not report `AlreadyExists`. ## Adversarial code review complete

🖥️ Harness: [pi] — reviewers `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash:max` (A) and `opencode-go/minimax-m3:max` (B).

**MAX_ROUNDS = 3** — derived, not chosen: the diff is 1302 insertions across 6 files, but counting only **non-test** lines (via the test-module boundary per file) gives **81 production code lines** → the 11-100 band → 3 rounds.

| Round | Reviewer A | Reviewer B | Unique issues | Character |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 13 | 8 | **15** | Two real bugs (fullwidth apostrophe not folded; sanitiser-rewritten titles missed by presence), a silent release-group drop, a discarded `try_init` failure, 3 README contradictions, 5 test-quality defects |
| 2 | 3 | 1 P1 + 2 P2 | **5** (1 refuted) | Missing apostrophe lookalikes (U+201A…); fixture wrote staging **outside** its temp dir; README over-claimed artist matching; 2 misleading comments |
| 3 | 4 | 1 | **5** | Signal test not `#[cfg(unix)]`; combining marks (U+0313/U+0314/U+05F3) still missed; README over-attributed `&`-folding; blank-title guard tested a different key than its comment claimed; my own now-inaccurate filter comment |

**All 25 round-1 to round-3 issues were fixed.** Notable ones the loop caught that I had missed:

- **A real second bug in my own fix**: filtering apostrophes *before* NFKC meant a fullwidth `＇` (U+FF07) never folded — the same duplicate-key failure, one keyboard away.
- **Dropping the sanitiser fold** silently re-broke the documented promise that a folder the write path named still satisfies the title it came from (`Album:Two` → stored `AlbumTwo`). I restored it with a second presence key, and proved the new test **bites** by reverting that helper (rc=101, restored byte-identical).
- **My test fixture wrote `downloads/staging` outside its temp dir** while its comment claimed otherwise — verified the leak on disk, fixed it, and hit a genuine follow-on bug (a duplicate `storage:` YAML key that broke the schedule child test), which the suite caught immediately.
- **A duplicate test I had added** in the tech-debt step duplicated an existing one.

Two reviewer claims I **rejected with measurement** rather than complying:

1. Round 2's **P1** — that `acquire_pid_lock` on a directory returns `IsADirectory`, so my test could not pass. Measured: `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY` on a directory returns **EEXIST** (POSIX checks `O_EXCL` first), and the test passes. I kept the test and made its comment cite that basis.
2. Round 1's **disc-marker asymmetry** — `(Disc 1)` vs `(Disc One)`: `strip_bracketed_annotations` drops any bracket without a listed edition word, so both fold identically. No asymmetry.

⚠️ **Max rounds (3) reached.** The final round found 5 issue(s) — the signal test's missing `#[cfg(unix)]`, the three missing combining/geresh marks, the README `&`-folding over-attribution, the blank-title guard/key mismatch, and my inaccurate filter comment. **All five were addressed, but reviewers had no round left to verify them**; two of them (the `#[cfg(unix)]` gate and the guard change) are behavioural rather than cosmetic, so manual review is recommended before proceeding.

**Final state:** `cargo fmt --check` clean, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` 0 issues, `cargo check --all-targets` 0 warnings, **934 lib + 35 bin + 241 other tests, 0 failures**. Only the intended 6 files are modified, and the leaked test artifact was removed.

**Known residual, deliberately not fixed here:** a **pre-existing** lib test in `src/runner.rs` — a file *not* in this diff — creates the default relative `downloads/staging` because it does not pin `storage.staging_dir` to a temp dir. ## Summary of changes on branch main

- **Fixed the reported duplication.** Album *presence* and MusicBrainz target dedupe now use the same album identity the search side already used, so `Sgt. Pepper’s` (U+2019), `Sgt. Pepper's` (ASCII) and `Sgt. Peppers` are one album rather than three. Previously the library's apostrophe-less tag matched neither of MusicBrainz's two Sgt. Pepper release groups, so a single discover run judged the album missing twice, searched twice, and downloaded it into two new folders beside the copy already on disk.
- **Closed the same gap class elsewhere.** Artist identity keys now fold apostrophe variants — including lookalikes with no Unicode decomposition (`‚`, `ʻ`, `ʼ`, the combining forms, Hebrew geresh) and the fullwidth `＇` — so the library's `Guns 'n' Roses` resolves against MusicBrainz's `Guns N’ Roses`. Presence also gained a sanitiser-folded key, so a folder the write path fused (`Album:Two` → `AlbumTwo`, or a title reduced to the `_` placeholder) still counts as the title it came from.
- **Kept the deliberate distinctions.** Edition markers (deluxe, remaster, live, remix, …) still separate an edition from the plain album, and unrelated titles stay separate. A release group dropped by the new identity dedupe is now logged with both MBIDs instead of vanishing silently.
- **Made the binary's startup path testable without changing its behaviour.** `main()` parses argv and `run(cli)` is drivable from tests; logging uses `try_init` and reports a failure instead of dying silently on a second call; a bin-local client-factory seam lets a test double reach the post-login wiring. Production still builds `RealClient::from_config` and still opens the database before taking the PID lock.
- **Test and documentation work.** Regression tests pin the reported case through the real scanner and the real release-group MBIDs. Coverage rose to `client.rs` 95.6 %, `db.rs` 97.5 %, `discover.rs` 99.1 %, `main.rs` 95.3 %, total **97.40 %**. **Checklist 3 complete.** One important finding for the design: `search.default_mode` is a *field with a schema default that is serialised into every generated `seakarr.yml`*, so essentially every existing install's config contains `default_mode: auto`. That makes the migration load-bearing rather than a convenience.

**Checklist 4 — implementation approaches:**

I see three ways to land this, differing mainly in where the compatibility lives:

1. **One canonical vocabulary, migrate the file at load (recommended).** The CLI accepts only `upgrade|manual|batch|discover` and rejects `auto` with a message naming `upgrade`. `reconcile_config_file` gains a `migrate_search_mode_value` step built exactly like the existing `migrate_rename`/`migrate_schedule_section` helpers (mutate the parsed YAML, report whether it changed, OR into the existing `renamed` flag), so the existing backup → rewrite → `config reconciled with current schema` path does the work. Identifiers (`SearchMode::Upgrade`, `ExecutionPlan::Upgrade`, `run_upgrade_mode`), error strings, doc comments and README all follow. *Trade-off:* one larger atomic diff, and the config file is rewritten — but that already happens for schema drift, and the `.bak` preserves the original.
2. **Translate in the resolver, leave the file alone.** The resolver maps `"auto"` to `Upgrade` with a warning while the CLI rejects it. *Trade-off:* no config-write path change, but every existing config keeps the stale value and warns on every run, and the CLI and config would disagree about whether `auto` is legal.
3. **Migrate the file, but keep `--mode auto` working with a deprecation warning** (the `--daemon` pattern). *Trade-off:* nothing breaks immediately, but it contradicts your decision to reject `auto`, and the ambiguous alias survives another release.

content.text:
## Design — rename `--mode auto` to `--mode upgrade`

Four sections. I'm putting them in one message and asking once (rather than stacking per-section questions, which the harness steering forbids) — flag any section you want changed and I'll revise it.

### 1. Behaviour — the contract

**CLI.** `--mode` accepts `upgrade | manual | batch | discover`; the arg's help text becomes `Override search mode (upgrade|manual|batch|discover)`. Two error strings replace the single one today:

- retired value: `invalid search mode 'auto'; this mode is now called 'upgrade'`
- any other invalid value: `invalid search mode '{value}' (must be upgrade, manual, batch, or discover)`

**Config migration.** `reconcile_config_file` gains a `migrate_search_mode_value` step built exactly like the existing helpers (mutate the parsed YAML, return whether it changed, OR into the `renamed` flag, before the merge):

- `search.default_mode` equal to `auto` after `trim()` — the same comparison the resolver uses, so migration and resolution can never disagree — is rewritten to `upgrade`.
- Any other value (typo, blank) is left alone for the resolver to reject, unchanged.
- The existing path then does the rest: `seakarr.yml.bak` holds the pre-migration file, the config is rewritten with the canonical header and the full schema, and `config reconciled with current schema (backup: …)` is logged at INFO. Already-no-op when the value is already `upgrade` (the `merged == file_value && !renamed` guard).
- A read-only config directory fails with the **existing** typed errors (`failed to back up config to …` / `failed to write migrated config: …`) — the same class of failure schema drift already produces, so no new behaviour.
- `default_mode`'s schema default becomes `upgrade`, so a freshly generated config never contains the retired value. This matters because every generated `seakarr.yml` serialises that default — without the migration, essentially every existing install would fail at startup.

### 2. Rename surface

- **Identifiers:** `SearchMode::Auto` → `Upgrade`, `ExecutionPlan::Auto` → `Upgrade`, `runner::run_auto_mode` → `run_upgrade_mode`, and the `main.rs` dispatch arm. `SearchMode` has **no consumers outside `mode.rs`** (verified), so that rename is contained; `ExecutionPlan::Upgrade` is referenced by the dispatcher and tests.
- **Strings:** both conflict messages (`--batch-file must not be blank in upgrade mode; use --mode batch`, `blank CLI selector is incompatible with upgrade mode; use --mode manual`) and `configured_mode_conflict`'s `incompatible with auto mode` text.
- **Doc comments / prose naming the mode:** `mode.rs`, `runner.rs`, `config.rs` (`library_upgrade.enabled` "auto mode only", `scan_on_startup`, `peer_track_count`, the `search.default_mode` docs), `scanner.rs` ("auto-mode upgrade destination/root/copies"), `filter.rs` (library-track-count notes), `discover.rs`/`discs.rs`/`organizer.rs` where they mean the mode, plus the CLI help text.
- **Deliberately untouched:** occurrences of "auto" that do not mean the mode — `client.rs`'s "never auto-retried" (4×) and similar. The sweep must be token-aware, not `s/auto/upgrade/`.
- **README:** the mode list and `--mode` references, the `search.default_mode` row and default, `library_upgrade.enabled`, `peer_track_count`, `scan_on_startup`, and the FAQ line that already reads *either upgrading what you have (`--mode auto`)*. Frozen specs under `docs/agent/specs/` stay as historical records (repo convention).
- **Tests to update:** `mode.rs` fixtures/assertions, `tests/mode_resolution_test.rs`, `tests/pipeline_test.rs`, and the `runner.rs` tests calling `run_auto_mode`.

### 3. Testing and verification

- `mode.rs` units: `--mode auto` rejected with the rename-pointing message; `upgrade` resolves to `ExecutionPlan::Upgrade` (the existing `configured_auto_without_selectors_returns_auto` becomes the upgrade equivalent); the conflict tests move to `upgrade`; the invalid-value test asserts the new list.
- `config.rs` migration tests alongside the existing ones: a file with `default_mode: auto` is rewritten to `upgrade` **and** `seakarr.yml.bak` is created; a file already saying `upgrade` is untouched with **no** backup; a whitespace-padded `auto` migrates (matching the resolver's `trim()`); an unrelated typo is left in place and still rejected by the resolver.
- Regression: load a config containing `default_mode: auto`, assert the in-memory config reports `upgrade` and the file on disk reads `upgrade`.
- Follow the repo's gates: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, full `cargo test`, coverage ≥95 % on changed files, markdownlint on the README, pre-commit.
- Release impact: MINOR bump (a breaking CLI rename on a pre-1.0 crate, matching the last release's convention). Scripts using `--mode auto` now fail loudly with a pointer; configs migrate silently on first run.

### 4. Out of scope

- Accepting `auto` anywhere — no alias, no deprecation warning, no shim.
- Renaming the `library_upgrade` config section, the `needs_upgrade` concept, or anything else that already says "upgrade".
- Changing what the mode does, its selectors, or the quality/upgrade rules.
- Naming the YAML source line for *arbitrary* invalid mode values (only the `auto` hint is added; the existing `find_default_mode_line` machinery stays as-is for conflicts).

I then write and commit the spec and hand it to you for review.

# Rename `--mode auto` to `--mode upgrade`

## Problem

`auto` names the mode by its least informative property. The mode walks the library, matches
each album against the `filters` targets, and re-downloads the ones whose format or bitrate
falls below them. The README already describes it that way ("either upgrading what you
have", `README.md:1149`), and the config section that drives it is already called
`library_upgrade`. Every other mode names what it does (`manual`, `batch`, `discover`), so
`auto` is the one value an operator has to look up.

The rename is not a string change alone. `search.default_mode` is a field whose serde
default is serialised into every generated `seakarr.yml` (`src/config.rs:92-93`), via
`default_search_mode()` (`src/config.rs:358`). An existing installation's config therefore
almost certainly contains `default_mode: auto`. Rejecting the retired value without
migrating the file would make every existing install fail at startup on its next run.

## Goal

One spelling, `upgrade`, in every layer - the CLI flag, the config value, the error text,
the README, and the Rust identifiers - with the retired value rejected loudly on the
command line and migrated in place in the config file.

## Scope

In scope:

- `--mode auto` is rejected with a message naming `upgrade`.
- `search.default_mode: auto` is migrated to `upgrade` during config reconciliation.
- The schema default for `search.default_mode` becomes `upgrade`.
- `SearchMode::Auto` -> `SearchMode::Upgrade`, `ExecutionPlan::Auto` ->
  `ExecutionPlan::Upgrade`, `runner::run_auto_mode` -> `runner::run_upgrade_mode`.
- Every user-facing string and doc comment that names the mode, including `README.md`.
- Tests updated, plus new tests for the rejection and for the migration.

Out of scope:

- Accepting `auto` anywhere: no alias, no deprecation warning, no shim.
- Renaming anything that already says "upgrade" (`library_upgrade`, `needs_upgrade`).
- Changing what the mode does, its selectors, or the quality rules.
- Naming the YAML source line for arbitrary invalid mode values.

## Decisions

Three decisions were taken with the operator before this spec was written.

1. **The CLI rejects the retired value** rather than aliasing it, so the ambiguity the
   rename removes cannot survive, and the error teaches the new name at the point of use.
2. **The config value is migrated automatically** rather than rejected, because a scheduled
   run must not break on a file the tool itself generated.
3. **The rename reaches every layer**, so flag, config, errors, documentation and
   identifiers all say the same thing.

## Architecture

### `src/mode.rs` - the resolver

`SearchMode` (`src/mode.rs:6`) and `ExecutionPlan` (`src/mode.rs:15`) rename their `Auto`
variants to `Upgrade`, and `ExecutionPlan::mode` (`src/mode.rs:32`) follows. The mode match
(`src/mode.rs:116`) keeps four arms, with `"upgrade" => SearchMode::Upgrade` replacing
`"auto" => SearchMode::Auto`.

The retired value gets its own arm ahead of the fall-through, so the message can point at
the replacement:

```text
invalid search mode 'auto'; this mode is now called 'upgrade'
```

The generic message keeps its existing shape, with `upgrade` first in the list
(`src/mode.rs:122`):

```text
invalid search mode '{value}' (must be upgrade, manual, batch, or discover)
```

Both `SearchMode::Upgrade` conflict messages (`src/mode.rs:148-156`) and the
`configured_mode_conflict` helper's `incompatible with auto mode` text (`src/mode.rs:79`)
are reworded to "upgrade mode". The helper keeps naming the YAML source and line through
`find_default_mode_line` (`src/config.rs:521`) when the mode came from the config.

`SearchMode` has no consumers outside `mode.rs`, so its rename is contained to that file
and its tests. `ExecutionPlan::Upgrade` is consumed by the dispatcher and by tests.

Sweep note: the rename must be token-aware. `src/client.rs:302`, `:501`, `:1299` and
`:1307` say "auto-retried" and mean something unrelated; a blind substring replacement
would corrupt them.

### `src/config.rs` - the migration and the default

`reconcile_config_file` (`src/config.rs:710`) already runs migrations on the parsed file
before merging it with the schema defaults:

```rust
let renamed = migrate_schedule_section(&mut file_value, config_file)?
    | migrate_rename(&mut file_value, "filters", "min_bitrate", "min_bit_rate")
    ...
```

A **value** migration joins that chain, built to the same contract as `migrate_rename`
(`src/config.rs:1070`): mutate the parsed YAML in place and report whether anything
changed.

`migrate_search_mode_value(&mut file_value) -> bool` rewrites `search.default_mode` when its
value, after `trim()`, equals `auto`. The comparison is deliberately the same one the
resolver makes (`--mode` if given, else `default_mode`, then `trim()`), so the migration can
never rewrite a value the resolver would accept or leave one it would reject.

Only that one value is touched. A blank, misspelled or otherwise unknown value is left in
place for the resolver to reject, unchanged.

The existing machinery then completes the work with no further changes:

- the `merged == file_value && !renamed` guard (`src/config.rs:738`) keeps an
  already-canonical config a true no-op: no rewrite, no backup;
- a change copies the original to `seakarr.yml.bak` (`src/config.rs:746`) and rewrites the
  file with the canonical header;
- `config reconciled with current schema (backup: ...)` records the event at INFO
  (`src/config.rs:755`).

`default_search_mode()` (`src/config.rs:358`) returns `"upgrade"` instead of `"auto"`, so a
newly generated config never contains the retired value.

### `src/main.rs` - the CLI surface

The `--mode` argument's help text (`src/main.rs:83`) becomes
`Override search mode (upgrade|manual|batch|discover)`, and the dispatcher's
`ExecutionPlan::Auto` arm (`src/main.rs:562`) calls `runner::run_upgrade_mode`.

### `src/runner.rs` and the prose that names the mode

`run_auto_mode` (`src/runner.rs:1403`) becomes `run_upgrade_mode`. Doc comments and comments
that name the mode are reworded in:

- `src/config.rs` - the `library_upgrade.enabled` text, `scan_on_startup`,
  `peer_track_count`, and the `search.default_mode` docs;
- `src/scanner.rs:411`, `:459`, `:583`, `:1324`, `:1539`, `:1604` - the "auto-mode upgrade
  destination/root/copies" wording;
- `src/filter.rs:7`, `:106`, `:165`, `:2112` - the library-track-count notes;
- `src/discover.rs`, `src/discs.rs` and `src/organizer.rs` where the word means the mode.

### Documentation and wording

`README.md`: the mode list and every `--mode` reference, the `search.default_mode` table row
and its default, the `library_upgrade.enabled` row ("auto mode only"), the `peer_track_count`
and `scan_on_startup` rows, and the FAQ line that reads "either upgrading what you have
(`--mode auto`)" (`README.md:1149`).

Historical specs under `docs/agent/specs/` are frozen records and are not edited.

## Data flow

Startup, in order:

1. `main` parses `--mode`, or leaves it unset.
2. `Config::load` reads `seakarr.yml`; `reconcile_config_file` runs its migrations, including
   `migrate_search_mode_value`. A retired value is rewritten to `upgrade` here, after the
   backup is written, so the returned `Config` already reports `upgrade`.
3. `resolve_execution_plan` reads `cli.mode` when given, otherwise
   `config.search.default_mode`. `--mode auto` fails here; `upgrade` yields
   `ExecutionPlan::Upgrade`.
4. The dispatcher calls `run_upgrade_mode`.

Because the migration runs before any resolution, a config that carried the retired value
behaves exactly like one that always said `upgrade`.

## Error handling

- **Retired CLI value:** `SeakarrError::Config` with the rename-pointing message, exit 1
  through the existing `exit_code_after_run` path. The same failure shape as any other
  invalid mode today.
- **Other invalid values:** unchanged message shape, with `upgrade` substituted for `auto`
  in the list.
- **Migration I/O failures:** the existing typed errors (`failed to back up config to ...`,
  `failed to write migrated config: ...`). A read-only config directory therefore fails the
  run, which it already does for schema drift, so this adds no new failure class.
- The migration cannot panic: it pattern-matches the parsed YAML and leaves anything
  unexpected in place.

## Backward compatibility

- `--mode auto` stops working, deliberately and loudly: any script using it fails with a
  message naming the replacement.
- `search.default_mode: auto` keeps working silently: the first run rewrites it to `upgrade`
  and preserves the previous file as `seakarr.yml.bak`.
- Rust API: `SearchMode::Auto` and `ExecutionPlan::Auto` disappear and `run_auto_mode` is
  renamed. `mode`, `runner` and `config` are public modules, so this is a breaking change for
  library consumers - which is why the release is a MINOR bump on this pre-1.0 crate,
  matching the convention of the previous release.
- Nothing else in the config schema changes.

## Deliberate limits

- No alias, no deprecation warning, no transitional period. The operator chose a hard rename;
  a shim would keep the ambiguous name alive and the flag and config would have different
  policies.
- The migration fixes one value only. It is not a general table of retired mode names, so a
  future rename adds its own step.
- An unknown value is never silently coerced. Only the exact retired spelling migrates, so
  typos stay visible.
- The mode's behaviour, selectors and quality rules are untouched.

## Testing

`src/mode.rs`:

- `--mode auto` is rejected and the message names `upgrade`.
- `upgrade` resolves to `ExecutionPlan::Upgrade`, from the CLI and from the config.
- The existing conflict tests move to `upgrade` and still identify the YAML source when the
  mode came from the config.
- An unknown value reports the new list, with `upgrade` first.

`src/config.rs`:

- A config containing `default_mode: auto` loads with `default_mode == "upgrade"`, the file
  on disk reads `upgrade`, and `seakarr.yml.bak` holds the pre-migration contents.
- A config already saying `upgrade` is untouched and creates no backup.
- A whitespace-padded `auto` migrates, matching the resolver's `trim()`.
- An unrelated invalid value is left in place and still rejected by the resolver.

Integration and regression:

- `tests/mode_resolution_test.rs` and `tests/pipeline_test.rs` are updated to the new
  vocabulary.
- The `src/runner.rs` tests that call `run_auto_mode` follow the rename.
- A regression test proves the retired value cannot reach the resolver from a migrated file:
  load the config, resolve the plan, and assert it is `Upgrade`.

Gates, as this repository requires: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, the
full `cargo test`, coverage to the 95 percent floor on the changed files,
`markdownlint README.md`, and `pre-commit run --all-files`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `--mode upgrade` selects the mode; `--mode auto` fails with a message naming `upgrade`.
2. A config containing `default_mode: auto` migrates to `upgrade` on first load, keeps
   `seakarr.yml.bak`, and the run proceeds normally.
3. `search.default_mode`'s default is `upgrade` in a freshly generated config.
4. No occurrence of `auto` that means this mode survives in `src/`, `tests/` or `README.md`,
   and the unrelated "auto-retried" wording in `src/client.rs` is untouched.
5. Every gate listed in Testing passes.

## Documentation

`README.md` is updated wherever it names the mode, so a reader finds `upgrade` and no stale
`auto`.

## Alternatives considered

**Translate in the resolver instead of migrating the file.** The resolver could accept `auto`
as a synonym and warn. Rejected: every existing config would keep the retired value, the
warning would repeat on every scheduled run, and the CLI and the config would disagree about
which spellings are legal.

**Keep `--mode auto` as a deprecated alias, following the `--daemon` pattern.** Rejected: the
operator asked for the name to be unambiguous, and an alias keeps the ambiguous name accepted
for at least another release.

**Migrate the value but leave the Rust identifiers alone.** Rejected: the flag would say
`upgrade` while `run_auto_mode` and `SearchMode::Auto` still said `auto`, which is the
confusion the rename exists to remove.

1. Accept `upgrade` and make it the default (resolver arm, `default_search_mode()`, `--mode` help).

6. Update the README, verified by grep plus markdownlint.
7. Verify all five acceptance criteria and run every gate (fmt, clippy, full suite, coverage ≥95 %, markdownlint, pre-commit) — no commit.

The ordering is deliberate and recorded in the plan: `upgrade` is accepted *before* `auto` is rejected, because rejecting first would break the shipped default that every generated config contains and take the suite red mid-plan. Every task ends green.

The only fixture that combines an *earlier firing migration* with the retired value already exists — `test_load_migrates_old_filter_keys_to_new_names` (`src/config.rs:1919`, fixture line `1939` has both `min_bitrate`/`min_bitdepth` and `default_mode: auto`) — but it asserts only the filter keys (`:2003-2009`), never the mode. Why it matters: converting the chain to `||` (a plausible refactor, since only "did anything change" is consumed) would silently skip the value migration for configs that also carry a legacy key, rewrite the file *keeping* `default_mode: auto`, and fail the run on the retired-value error — with no test going red. Smallest fix: one line in that existing test, e.g. `assert_eq!(config.search.default_mode, "upgrade");`.
2. **P2 — report-only (spec-accepted): the migration now makes the first post-upgrade run write to the config directory even for a previously canonical file.** `Config::load` runs in `main()` and again in `run_with`, ahead of the mode check, so an existing install whose file was generated by v0.28.0 (`default_mode: auto`, otherwise schema-canonical, previously a true no-op) is backed up and rewritten on the next invocation; with a read-only config directory/volume the run now fails with `failed to back up config to ...` where it previously started. The spec's error-handling section explicitly accepts this ("adds no new failure class"), and the README row (`README.md:270`) says "keeps loading", which is true only for a writable config directory. No code change requested; flagging so the wording/behaviour trade-off is a conscious one.
3. **P2 — report-only nit: two "automatic" phrasings survive the vocabulary sweep.** `README.md:124` (`# One-shot automatic upgrade scan`) and `src/discover.rs:776` ("manual and automatic placement never fired on a real library"). Neither is a mode identifier — the spec's criterion 4 targets identifiers, and `automatic_place_target` is deliberately kept — so this may be intentional; `README.md:124` would read more consistently as `# One-shot upgrade scan`.

### Merge verdict: **OK with notes.** Both mandated behaviours are correct in the code and covered by tests that fail when the change is reverted (CLI rejection naming the replacement; config `auto → upgrade` during reconciliation with a `.bak`). I found no P0/P1 defect and no issue caused by this diff beyond the three P2 notes above.

Tests pass (**943 lib + 36 bin + 13 + 3 + 4 + 186 + 35 + 0 + 3, 0 failures**, exit 0). Environment: **normal repo** (`GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON`), branch **`main`** = the default branch, local `main` **2 commits ahead** of `origin/main` (the spec and plan commits) with 12 modified files uncommitted and 0 staged.

🖥️ Commit mode: **automated**.

## Summary of changes on branch main

- **Renamed the `auto` search mode to `upgrade` in every layer.** The CLI value, the config value, the error text, the README and the Rust identifiers (`SearchMode::Upgrade`, `ExecutionPlan::Upgrade`, `runner::run_upgrade_mode`) all now use one vocabulary, because `auto` never told an operator what the mode does — it scans the library and re-downloads albums whose format or bitrate falls below the configured targets.
- **The retired value is handled deliberately on each side.** `--mode auto` is now **rejected** with a message naming `upgrade` (a breaking CLI change), while an existing `seakarr.yml` carrying `search.default_mode: auto` **keeps loading**: reconciliation rewrites it to `upgrade` and preserves the original as `seakarr.yml.bak`. The schema default is now `upgrade`, so a freshly generated config never contains the retired value.
- **No behaviour changed beyond the name.** The `SearchMode::Upgrade` validation arm is the old `Auto` arm with new text, the dispatcher calls the same runner, and the mode's rules are untouched. The one functional difference is the default value, which names the same mode the old `auto` did.
- **Documentation and tests follow the rename.** The README documents the new name, the migration and the CLI rejection; doc comments across `config.rs`, `scanner.rs`, `filter.rs`, `discover.rs`, `organizer.rs`, `main.rs` and `runner.rs` were corrected, while unrelated wording (`client.rs`'s "auto-retry", the `automatic_place_target` helper) was deliberately left alone. Tests gained a migration regression, an end-to-end CLI-rejection test, the positive CLI-path test and a cross-migration pin.
- **Verification behind it:** full suite 943 lib + 36 bin + 13 + …, 0 failures; coverage 97.39 % lines; `clippy -D warnings`, `fmt`, `cargo audit`, `cargo deny`, `markdownlint` and `pre-commit` all clean.

**Two things carried forward rather than glossed over.** First, the review loop reached its 3-round cap, so it emitted `COMPLETE` rather than `CLEAN`: round 3's three P2 findings (an unpinned `|`-vs-`||` migration chain, the README's wording for a read-only config directory, and two residual "automatic" phrasings) were all fixed, two of them proven by mutation — but no reviewer round remained to verify them.
